summary: Baraa bin Aazib says he delayed for two years before asking the Prophet a question, out of the awe he felt for him.

Zuhri relays that the Sahabah raced to collect the Prophet's saliva and leftover wudhu water for blessing, and the Prophet told them that whoever loves to be loved by Allaah and His Messenger must speak the truth, return trusts and not harm his neighbour.
new_themes: seeking blessings from the Prophet's remains
notes: Zuhri relays an unnamed source of unquestioned reliability, who is not tagged.

summary: Urwa bin Mas'ood, sent to negotiate at Hudaybiyyah, describes how closely the Sahabah honoured the Prophet, and tells his people he has never seen any ruler's followers so devoted to their leader.
new_themes: seeking blessings from the Prophet's remains
notes: Opens with a cross-reference to the report of Miswar and Marwaan, which is not told here. Najaashi is tagged as the King of Abyssinia, as the text gives no name.

summary: Abu Quraad Sulami says the Sahabah drank the water dripping from the Prophet's wudhu, and the Prophet told them that loving Allaah and His Messenger means keeping trusts, speaking truth and being kind to neighbours.
new_themes: seeking blessings from the Prophet's remains
notes: The heading names Abdur Rahmaan bin Haarith as the reporter, but the text is Abu Quraad's own account, so only he is tagged.

summary: Aamir reports that Abdullaah bin Zubayr drank the blood the Prophet had cupped out, and the Prophet foretold strife for him and for the people because of it; a separate note says popular opinion linked his great strength to that blood.
new_themes: seeking blessings from the Prophet's remains
notes: Two reports: Aamir's account from his father, then a separate note by Abu Moosa citing Abu Aasim. The heading repeats the story of the blood.

summary: Kaysaan reports that Salmaan saw Abdullaah bin Zubayr drinking from the Prophet's cupping blood, and the Prophet told him he would be spared the Fire except to pass over the Bridge, after foretelling strife for him.
new_themes: seeking blessings from the Prophet's remains
notes: Kaysaan was the freed slave of Abdullaah bin Zubayr. OCR garbles the Prophet's gesture line.

summary: Safeenah says the Prophet asked him to bury his cupping blood out of sight, but he drank it instead; when he told the Prophet, the Prophet only laughed.
new_themes: seeking blessings from the Prophet's remains

summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that his father Maalik bin Sinaan licked the Prophet's blood from his face after Uhud, and the Prophet said that once his blood had mixed with Maalik's, the Fire would never touch him.
new_themes: seeking blessings from the Prophet's remains

summary: Hakeemah bint Umaymah reports that the Prophet kept a wooden cup for urine under his bed, and when a maidservant drank from it, the Prophet said she had built a solid barrier against the Fire.
new_themes: seeking blessings from the Prophet's remains
notes: Hakeemah and Surah are not in the approved list, and their status as Companions is not confirmed. Surah is the maidservant of Ummu Salamah.

summary: Abu Ayyoob reports that he hosted the Prophet on the lower storey and worried about standing above him, and that the Prophet taught him dhikr with great reward; a second part says the Prophet sent back food containing garlic or onion.
notes: Two reports: the hosting and the dhikr, then a separate report about the dinner. OCR loss: the text jumps mid-sentence after 'You should recite:' and the dhikr formula is missing; check against the source.

summary: Abu Ayyoob asks the Prophet to move to the upper storey, since it is not proper for him to be above the Prophet, and the Prophet has his small luggage moved.
notes: Short variant of the report before it.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Umar had Abbaas's gutter removed after blood from it spoiled his clothes, and then told Abbaas to restore it exactly where the Prophet had placed it, even if he had to climb on Umar's back.
notes: A second report ('Another narration') says Umar carried Abbaas on his shoulders. OCR cuts off the sentence 'Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) then did Just'.

summary: Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan reports that Abdullaah bin Umar touched the place where the Prophet sat on his pulpit and then his own face, and Yazeed bin Abdullaah reports Sahabah taking sand from beside the Prophet's grave to make du'aa.

people.name: Ibraheem bin Abdur Rahmaan bin Abdul Qaari

notes: Two reports: Ibraheem's, then Yazeed's. The heading spells Abdullaah bin Umar's name with OCR errors.

summary: Abu Layla reports that Usayd bin Hudhayr, while joking with the Prophet, asked to be allowed retaliation for a poke, and when the Prophet lifted his garment, Usayd embraced him and kissed his sides.

Habbaan bin Waasi reports that at Badr the Prophet nudged Sawaad bin Ghuzayyah's belly with an arrow shaft, and when Sawaad asked for retaliation and kissed the Prophet's belly, the Prophet made du'aa for him.

Hasan reports that the Prophet jabbed a man wearing yellow dye with a date-palm branch, leaving a mark, and when the man asked for retaliation the Prophet bared his belly and the man kissed it, forgoing retribution on condition of the Prophet's intercession.
notes: 'Hadhrat Hasan' is taken as Hasan bin Abil Hasan from the approved list, which is a best reading and should be confirmed. The man who wore yellow dye is not named.

summary: Hasan reports that the Prophet prodded Sawaad bin Amr in the belly with a twig for wearing perfume, and the rest of the account is said to match the report above.
notes: Cut off: the rest is only referred back to the report above, so the account is incomplete here. The narrator is taken as Hasan bin Abil Hasan, as in n01336.

summary: Hasan reports that Sawaadah bin Amr wore so much Khalooq perfume that the Prophet shook it off his clothes, and after the Prophet lightly struck him with a twig he asked for retaliation, then kissed the Prophet, forgoing it on condition of intercession.
notes: Probably the same Companion as Sawaad bin Amr in n01337; the text spells the name Sawaadah. Narrator taken as Hasan bin Abil Hasan, as in n01336.

summary: This is a cross-reference saying that Talha bin Baraa embraced the Prophet and kissed his feet on meeting him, and that Abu Bakr's kiss on the Prophet's forehead at his death will be quoted later.
notes: Editorial cross-reference to reports given elsewhere in the book, not a narration in itself. Husayn bin Wahwah is named only as the source of an earlier report.

summary: Anas bin Maalik reports that when Madinah heard the Prophet had been martyred at Uhud, an Ansaari woman who had lost her father, son, husband and brother went looking for him, and on finding him safe said she no longer cared about her losses.
notes: The woman is not named.

summary: Zubayr reports that on the day of Uhud, when the women of Madinah heard that the Prophet had been martyred, one woman set out on foot to see for herself how he was.
notes: The woman is not named.

summary: Sa'd bin Abi Waqqaas reports that a woman of Banu Dinaar, whose husband, brother and father had all died at Uhud, asked after the Prophet and said that after seeing him every calamity seemed trivial.
notes: The woman is not named.

summary: Anas reports that during Uhud Abu Talha shielded the Prophet with his arrows and his own chest, asked him not to rise lest an arrow strike him, and offered to be sent on any task.
Qataadah bin Nu'maan says that after his bow broke during Uhud, he stood in front of the Prophet and turned his own face to take each arrow aimed at the Prophet's face.
notes: Cut off with '...'. The text says the rest is the same as the account in the chapter on Qataadah's bravery.

summary: Abu Sa'eed Khudri reports that in the Prophet's final illness he said he was standing at his Kowthar and that a servant of Allaah had chosen the Aakhirah over this world, and that only Abu Bakr understood and wept.

Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that after a revelation the Prophet told Faatima that his death was near, and she wept until he told her she would be the first of his family to join him, and then she laughed.
notes: The name of the Surah is missing from the OCR text. One of the Prophet's wives is unnamed.

summary: Aa'isha reports that during his final illness the Prophet whispered to Faatima, first making her weep and then making her laugh when he told her she would be the first of his family to join him.
notes: OCR garbles the end of the last sentence.

summary: Ummu Salamah reports that Faatima laughed because the Prophet had told her that she would lead the women of Jannah after Maryam, the daughter of Imraan.

Alaa reports that as the Prophet was about to pass away, Faatima wept, and he told her to say Innaa Lillaahi wa Innaa Ilayhi Raaji'oon, since every calamity is rewarded, and she asked whether this applied even to losing him.
notes: The narrator Alaa is not identified. The approved list has Alaa bin Hadhrami, but the link is not confirmed, so this entry is left unlinked for review.

summary: Mu'aadh bin Jabal reports that as the Prophet walked beside him on his way to Yemen, the Prophet told him he might not see him again and that those closest to him are the people of taqwa, wherever they are; Mu'aadh wept at the parting.
A short variant reports that the Prophet told Mu'aadh not to weep, because such weeping comes from Shaytaan.
notes: Short variant of n01350; the narrator is not named.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that when the Ansaar wept in the Masjid fearing the Prophet's death, he came out and said they would dwindle in number, and that whoever governs them should accept the good of their good people and excuse the evil of their wrongdoers.

Ummul Fadhl bint Haarith reports that she wept during his final illness fearing how they would be treated after his death, and the Prophet replied that they would be in a weaker position once he had left.
notes: '(to the Ummah)' is an editorial gloss in the source text.

summary: Abdullaah bin Mas'ood reports the Prophet's final instructions: he would be bathed by his closest family, shrouded in his own clothes, prayed over first by the angels, and placed in the grave by the men of his family.
notes: Aa'isha is mentioned as the owner of the room where the Prophet gathered them.

summary: Yazeed bin Baabnoos reports Aa'isha's account of the Prophet's last illness and death, Abu Bakr's kisses on his forehead and his speech that Muhammad had died while Allaah lives forever, and Umar then urging the people to pledge allegiance to Abu Bakr.
notes: Long composite account: a conversation with Aa'isha, her report of the death, then Abu Bakr's speech at the Masjid. An unnamed friend of the narrator is not tagged.

summary: Ali bin Abi Taalib reports the dispute over who would bury the Prophet, which Abu Bakr settled by saying that the family should decide who enters the room; a second report from Ali bin Husayn says the Ansaar also claimed the right.
notes: Two reports: Ali bin Abi Taalib, then a second introduced as a narration of Ali bin Husayn. The heading's narrator name is lost to OCR.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that Ali stayed with the Prophet as he died, and that Ali then washed the body with Fadhl bin Abbaas and an Ansaari, guided by a voice from the house to bathe him in his clothes.
notes: Contains an editorial footnote from the author (citing Ahmad, Ibn Sa'd and others) in the middle of the text.

summary: Abdullaah bin Abbaas reports that after the Prophet's death, groups of men entered the room and prayed the Janaazah salaah individually, with no one leading them, followed by the women, children and slaves.
Sahl bin Sa'd reports that once the Prophet was shrouded and placed on a bed in a corner of the room, people entered in groups to pray the Janaazah salaah, with no one leading them.
notes: The narrator's name is garbled in the text ('Hadhrat Sahl in Sa'd'); identified from the heading.

summary: Moosa bin Muhammad bin Ibraheem reports, from a book written by his father, that Abu Bakr and Umar greeted the Prophet and made du'aa at the front of the rows, with no one acting as imam.
notes: Taken from a written book, not an oral chain. The father is not named in the text, so he is not tagged.
